chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The gatherings are with the confidentiality.'
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the confidentiality of gatherings in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the sanctity of private discourse, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence to protect reputations and maintain social harmony. It underscores the moral obligation of attendees to act as trustworthy custodians of shared secrets, reflecting the broader Islamic ethic of preserving trust (amanah) in interpersonal relations.
